name: Lake Skimmer Hydrofoil
description: A small, fast hydrofoil designed for Great Lakes racing — an underground sport that draws Tier 2-4 thrill seekers and heavy betting. Skimmers ride on submerged foils that lift the hull clear of the water, reducing drag and allowing speeds that terrify passengers and thrill pilots. The racing circuit runs through the harbor, around the breakwater, and out into open lake in conditions that would make the harbor patrol blanch. Crashes are spectacular, frequent, and occasionally fatal.
autonomy: Manual only. The whole point is the pilot.
armament: None. Speed is the weapon and the defense.
common_usage: Lake racing, high-speed water transit, smuggling, showing off.
story_hooks: A lake racing champion disappears during a night race and their Skimmer is found drifting with the motor still running
The racing circuit's route takes pilots over a deep spot in the lake where instruments go haywire — and the fast ones feel something pull at their foils
related_entities: Kelpline Logistics TideRunner FR-12 Amphibious Surface Effect Shuttle
physical_description: A sleek, narrow hull of scarred composite and welded steel, maybe 16 feet stem to stern, with twin submerged foils angled like predatory fins. The cockpit is stripped to essentials—a reinforced pilot seat, exposed hydraulic lines, and a jury-rigged control column wrapped in grip tape and scars from a hundred near-misses. Salt-crusted, oil-stained, patched with mismatched plating; racing numbers spray-painted in fading phosphorescent green.
